utterance: Monday is a terrible name for a cat.
note: A weekday in a sentence about nothing temporal — the same trap Vesta's conditional time-context gate exists for.

utterance: What is the capital of Australia?
note: General knowledge. It belongs to the chat model, and the correct router answer is escalation.
Names a routing target that is on Vesta's roadmap and dispatchable by nothing today. Mentioning an automation system is not asking for one.

utterance: My alarm didn't go off yesterday.
note: Past tense, a complaint, and the word "alarm". Setting one here would be a false positive on a user who is annoyed about alarms.

utterance: I need to remember to set a timer later.
note: Contains the exact tool phrase. "I need to remember to X later" is a statement about an intention, not the request.

A grounded time in a past-tense report. The pair to slot.alarm.bare: there the time was invented and there was no request; here the time is real and there is still no request. Grounding cannot catch this one — it has to be classified correctly.

The same utterance as slot.followup.minutes with NO pending state supplied. It must not become a timer. This is the pair that proves the router reads the state Vesta gives it rather than inventing a context.
A name and the verb. Every required argument of make_call is present in the words; only the request is missing — and the cost of getting it wrong is a phone ringing.

utterance: The drive to Piazza Garibaldi took forever.
note: A destination in a past-tense complaint.

utterance: My calendar is a disaster this week.
note: get_calendar_events has NO required arguments, so grounding can refuse nothing here. Every no-required-argument tool is a false positive waiting to happen, and classification is the only defence.

utterance: Time really flies when you're busy.
note: Same shape as above, for get_time.
Explicit negation of the action it names. The required argument is also absent, so grounding would catch it too — but it must be classified correctly rather than rescued by a guard.

utterance: Don't call Marco, I'll do it myself.
note: The negation case where the guard CANNOT help: the contact is named, so a call proposal would be fully grounded. Negation has to be understood.

utterance: What would happen if I set a timer for zero minutes?

note: Speech-to-text picking up filler. The assist surface produces this and the router must not read intent into it.
